Two causes must show they are independent rather than one story counted twice. A conditional cause must show that the condition held, which is the strongest of the three because it explains the sequence the others merely report, and the most exposed, because a condition that cannot be evidenced leaves the draft with nothing at all.

questions.explanation: Each draft carries a different duty: ruling out alternatives, showing independence, or verifying the condition. The conditional draft does the most work and so faces the highest risk of failing its own test.
questions.hint: Ask what each draft must prove.
